rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: bite/sting with danger signs / Check for urgent bite/sting conditions
rule_level_problems.problem: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Deep bite wound" "morphologic abnormality")) is not a Clinical finding descendant; the same pattern as body-site concepts slipping past VHA's test. It will not match recorded findings. Use a disorder such as 'Deep mammalian bite wound'.
The bite/sting gate (Bite - wound OR Venomous sting) does not subsume 'Toxic effect of venom', so 'venom in eyes' without a recorded bite/sting never reaches Urgent and never triggers the check task.

Footnote 2 'shock likely' is not encoded as a probable rule; the priority rule uses a raw Shock finding instead of active_condition, so pulse >= 100, RR > 30, confusion/restlessness won't raise priority.
Actively bleeding is a plain Bleeding finding with no current/active qualifier, which is over-broad.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable papular urticaria after bite/sting
rule_level_problems.problem: Evidence is limited to Insect bite reaction, but the page branch covers spider bites too.

summary: Most consequential: 'Deep bite wound' is a morphologic abnormality used as a clinical_finding, so the deep-wound criterion cannot match; and venom in eyes is gated behind a bite/sting finding it is not a child of, so ocular venom exposure alone is not made Urgent. Footnote 2's 'shock likely' has no probable rule. Anaphylaxis, cellulitis, papular urticaria and most red-box criteria are otherwise encoded faithfully.
